summary: 4 findings for the connection wait of a failed turn: 2 confirmed by failing tests and now fixed (F1: a scheduled retry that fired offline left no `network` marker; F4: a session change while a wait held did not end it, closed with a follow-up for the relaunch's wait, device paths and the continuation's own re-check), 1 refuted model error (F2); on the fixed code all 8 properties plus both liveness properties hold for 1 tab, 2 runs, 2 attempts, 1 network flap, 1 session move, one relaunch (2.8M states, depth 74; 14.5M states with 2 flaps), and every property but the TypeOK shape check has a mutation that fails it (15 of 15 DETECTED, including the bugs as mutations).

modeled: ConnectivityMonitor verify (one shared probe per host), #check, #reachable, the #attempt recovery loop, report, #set -> connectivityChanged -> flush
the pool facts the rules read: running, lastRun, stopped, session/touched, awaitingConnection, as pool events that each end in sync()
abstracted: one tab, one host name, one session counter; four outcome kinds (dns, net, transient, fatal)
time is order only: any armed timer may fire at any moment
sync() and flush() are synchronous regions run as ordered micro-steps under one program counter
the retry RPC is one atomic send
out_of_scope: an online launch's continuation and the rest of the relaunch past its offline wait, stock auto-retry takeover, the wake window, hosted tabs, quit freeze, tab close, retry.enabled toggling
the duration of the retry RPC (a user prompt while it is in flight is stock's), two tabs at once, attempt counts above 2
assumptions: A1: every pool event that changes a fact is followed by TurnResume.sync() before the next macrotask; setAwaitingConnection does not call sync()
A2/A3/A4: sync() and flush() run in one macrotask; a ready sidecar resolves whenReady in a microtask and Boot continues every waiting #run in that macrotask
A5: a run cannot be live on an omp that is not up (the F2 model fix)
A7: strong fairness per component, and the network eventually comes back (an assumption, not code)

properties.name: NoRetryIntoUserRun
properties.meaning: Stock retry is never sent while the tab's live run is one the user started.
properties.source: src/main/turn-resume.ts:511-521; turn-resume.test.ts 'a prompt sent during the wait replaces it'
properties.bounds: Tabs={t1}, MaxStarts=2, MaxAttempts=2, MaxFlaps=1 (2 in the deep run), MaxSess=1, MaxCancels=1

properties.name: NoRetryAfterCallOff
properties.meaning: Cancel, Stop, a new prompt or a session/branch change during a probe (or while a retry is armed) never leads to a later retry of that failure.
properties.source: src/main/turn-resume.ts:572-585; turn-resume.test.ts '%s while the lookup is probed ends it'

properties.name: WaitEnds
properties.meaning: A wait row always ends once the network is back.
properties.bounds: Tabs={t1}, MaxStarts=1, MaxAttempts=1, MaxFlaps=1, MaxSess=0, MaxCancels=0; strong fairness per component, network heals (assumption). A larger run (MaxStarts=2, 158504 states, 308 s) also holds.

properties.name: MarkerNetwork
properties.statement: MarkerNetwork == pc = "idle" => \A t \in Tabs : awaiting[t] => store[t] = "network"
properties.meaning: While a wait holds, the marker file says `network`, so a crash during the wait still retries.
properties.bounds: same as NoRetryIntoUserRun (violated before F1's fix, FireSyncs=FALSE, evidence TurnResume-MC_marker.log)

properties.name: OneOfWaitOrScheduled
properties.meaning: A tab has at most one of: a held wait, a probe, a scheduled retry.

properties.name: OneProbePerHost
properties.meaning: One probe is in flight for the host; concurrent asks share it.
properties.bounds: same as NoRetryIntoUserRun (one tab: consecutive asks of the same tab, not two tabs)

properties.name: OfflineOnlyOnNoAnswer
properties.meaning: The monitor goes offline through a probe only when neither the failed host nor the default way out answered.

properties.name: NoRetryAfterSessionChangeWhileHeld
properties.meaning: A session or branch change while a wait HOLDS ends the wait and never leads to a retry (found by the verifier as F4, adopted as the rule on 28 Oct 2026).
properties.source: the user's decision on F4; the probe and the scheduled retry already checked the session and touched count (turn-resume.ts:584-585, #holds); the held wait now does (#movedSince, turn-resume.ts:525-528, 766-771)
properties.bounds: same as NoRetryIntoUserRun (violated before F4's fix, evidence TurnResume-MC_held.log)

findings.title: A scheduled retry that fires while offline leaves no `network` marker
findings.story: A turn ends in a transient error (a 503) while the link is up: #judge plans a scheduled retry and #arm shows its row. Before the 30 s timer fires the connection drops (report(false)). The timer runs #fire: stillHolds passes, stock retry.enabled is read, then `!network.online`, so #fire releases the row, records the attempt and calls #hold(tab, "retry"): the wait row shows (setAwaitingConnection(true)). #fire returns there and never calls sync(), so deriveMarkers has not run and the marker file has no entry for the tab: a scheduled retry writes none, and awaitingConnection is only turned into the `network` reason by a sync. Nothing syncs until some later run-state change. If OMPdesk crashes or is killed while the tab waits, the relaunch finds no marker and the turn is never continued. #verifyNetwork's own hold calls sync() with the comment "a crash during the wait still retries"; #fire's does not.

reproduction.test: src/main/turn-resume.test.ts::TurnResume connection wait (formal/turn-resume) > a scheduled retry that fires while offline hands over to the connection wait, and the marker file says `network` (a crash during the wait still retries)

fix.summary: #fire calls this.sync() right after #hold in its offline branch (turn-resume.ts:704-708), so deriveMarkers writes the `network` marker while the wait holds. Every other #hold caller already ran inside sync() or synced after it. Model: FireSyncs is gone, FireResume always runs the sync chain; the bug is the mutation fire-hold-without-sync.

findings.title: A session or branch change while the wait holds does not end it; stock retry runs in the new session
findings.story: This is a property the verifier added, not one of the stated ones; whether the behavior is intended is a design question. While offline a turn fails on the network: #judge holds it, the wait row shows and the marker says `network`. The user switches the tab to another session or branch (noteTouched bumps `touched`, sync()). #watchScheduledRetry and #verifyNetwork's continuation compare sessionFile and `touched` and end the retry or the probe; the held wait is not looked at (#judge only ends it for a new run or Cancel). The connection returns, flush() runs #run(tab, "retry") and stock retry is sent to a tab that now shows another session or branch.

reproduction.test: src/main/turn-resume.test.ts::TurnResume connection wait (formal/turn-resume) > %s while the connection wait holds ends the wait, and nothing retries into the new session once online

fix.summary: The user's call: the held wait follows the probe and the scheduled retry. #hold records what the wait holds for (HeldWait.since: session file and touched, from the failed fact, the probe, the armed retry or, since the follow-up, the relaunch's tab) and #judge ends a wait whose tab moved (#movedSince: touched differs, or the recorded session file is not the tab's) with #dropWait. Follow-up after the review of 3ba7f88be: the continuation re-checks too (flush hands `since` to #run, which looks before it starts the omp and once the omp is up; a fired scheduled retry's #run carries the armed session), a held tab's file move syncs the rules with no turn running (pool and host), a paired device's moves count (hosted tab's own touched; a view bumps its window tab's), `touched` counts only a move that worked (movesTab, after the response), and fork_from is no move. Model: wsg, Moved in S_NewRun/FlushStep/Boot, Launch and FileMoved; the bugs are the mutations held-wait-ignores-session-change, launch-hold-records-no-session, flush-skips-recheck and ready-skips-recheck.

findings.title: (Refuted, model error) a retry sent into a user's run through a prompt on an omp that is not ready
findings.story: The first model run ended a scheduled retry's #run waiting in whenReady (the tab's omp not ready), the omp became ready, the user's prompt started a run, and only then did the #run continue and send retry into it. Two steps cannot happen in the code: a run cannot be live on an omp that is not up, and whenReady's resolution is a microtask, so the continuation runs in the same macrotask as the status event, before any prompt. The model was wrong (it allowed a prompt on an omp that is not ready and ran the continuation as a separate step). Fixed in the model: a prompt needs a ready omp, Unready needs every tab idle, Boot continues every waiting #run. The property was not changed.

sanity_checks: before the fixes: MC_marker.cfg (FireSyncs=FALSE) violated MarkerNetwork and MC_held.cfg violated NoRetryAfterSessionChangeWhileHeld (TurnResume-MC_marker.log, TurnResume-MC_held.log); after them MC.cfg holds every invariant including both

the bugs are kept as mutations and DETECTED on the fixed model: fire-hold-without-sync fails MarkerNetwork; held-wait-ignores-session-change, launch-hold-records-no-session and flush-skips-recheck fail NoRetryAfterSessionChangeWhileHeld; ready-skips-recheck fails NoRetryAfterCallOff
NeverWaits, NeverRetries, NeverArmed, NeverProbing, NeverLaunchWaits are violated, so a wait, a retry, an armed retry, a probe row and a relaunch's wait are reachable
mutate.ts: 15 of 15 mutations DETECTED, no property UNCOVERED, only TypeOK waived (shape check)

one equivalent mutant kept as evidence, not in the set: dropping the sync() after #hold in #verifyNetwork's continuation is MISSED because the marker already says `network` since the probe row (formal/turn-resume/evidence/equivalent-mutant-verify-hold-without-sync.log)
deadlock checking is ON in every safety run (an explicit Terminated action exists), so a state with a stuck wait that is not quiescent is reported
deep run (MaxFlaps=2): 14470188 distinct states, depth 81, all invariants hold

scratch break (persist step A.5, before the fixes): dropping the session and touched checks from #verifyNetwork's continuation in turn-resume.ts and from the model's `holds` made `verify-all.ts formal --only turn-resume` FAIL on NoRetryAfterCallOff with the last rows tagged turn-resume.ts:557-580 and the drift line naming src/main/turn-resume.ts (formal/turn-resume/evidence/scratch-break-run.log); after dropping both edits the run PASSES with --strict-drift (formal/turn-resume/evidence/scratch-dropped-rerun.log)
